title: The quotient of a polynomial ring over a field by a separable polynomial is reduced
statement: Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field], $E[T]$ the polynomial ring in one indeterminate [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and $Q\in E[T]$ a separable polynomial [def-pc-separable-polynomial] (there are $U,V\in E[T]$ with $UQ+VQ'=1$). Then the quotient ring $E[T]/(Q)$ by the principal ideal generated by $Q$ is reduced: if $g\in E[T]$ and $g^m\in(Q)$ for some integer $m\ge1$, then $g\in(Q)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, label line 10152), first paragraph, line 10182: 'Since $P$ is separable this is a finite product of fields and we win' (here only the consequence 'reduced' is stated); tag 030U verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (line 3961)
